A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and describe the same SkyDiffusion/G2A-3 study, supporting comparison of text, equations, tables and figures. Both end with references on page 10; neither includes an appendix or embedded supplement despite referring to supplementary material.

before.justification: v3 reports original image-synthesis experiments on CVUSA, CVACT, VIGOR-Chicago and G2A-3, including quantitative comparisons, qualitative results and component ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains original image-synthesis results and reports revised comparisons and ablations in Tables 1–3 and accompanying figures.

M1.justification: v4 removes the complete optional DNCM lighting branch, its reference-image input and separate training stage from the described framework (Sections 3.2–3.3 and Figure 2). This removes a distinct inference capability. Curved-BEV geometry, multi-view fusion and the diffusion objective remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The three established benchmarks and all three G2A-3 tasks remain. Figure 4 switches from counting image pairs to individual images, explaining the doubled counts. Newly naming Boston and Los Angeles supplies geographical detail without establishing expanded coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 replaces HawkI with GPG2A across all three benchmarks. Standard-BEV controls are added to the ablation comparison. The G2A-3 qualitative figure drops its ControlNet column, although ControlNet remains in the quantitative comparison.

E3.justification: Section 4 changes the reported G2A-3 split from random 5:1 partitioning to regional 4:1 partitioning, substantially revising the generalization test across its three tasks. Ablations also introduce standard-BEV controls. Established benchmark splits, metrics and core training budgets remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v4 Table 2 adds standard-versus-curved BEV tests on CVACT and VIGOR-Chicago, addressing whether curvature helps beyond ordinary projection. It replaces v3 Table 3's explicit lighting ablations and separate unlit multi-view condition. G2A-3 case studies are revised, including a new historical crosswalk-change example. Promised lambda sensitivity experiments are not supplied.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Both present single numerical values for each method and metric.

E6.justification: Shared Table 1 scores are unchanged, but GPG2A and standard-BEV results are added and HawkI results removed. G2A-3 FIDs change from 114.64 to 96.16 for disaster scenes, 35.51 to 33.29 for historical imagery, and 32.11 to 32.53 for UAV imagery, under a revised reported split. v4's multi-view tuple, 31.90/0.205/11.15/0.651, exactly matches v3's multi-view-plus-light row, preventing interpretation as an unambiguous same-setting gain. Qualitative application results also change.

T1.justification: The DNCM operator and lighting-composition definition in v3 Equation 5 are removed. The curved-surface, projection, fusion and loss equations remain equivalent. v4's added forward-diffusion formula explains the existing process rather than introducing a new theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: BEV-guided synthesis, Curved-BEV and multi-to-one mapping, the three-task G2A-3 dataset, and state-of-the-art performance. The headline SSIM and FID improvement claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: v4 explains why lambda=0 supports planar multi-view fusion and discusses regional organization given uneven historical-year coverage. It expands disaster applicability to comparison with pre-disaster imagery and geolocalization. Lighting-specific interpretations disappear, while the limitation concerning faithful rooftop generation remains.

D1.justification: v4 newly discloses boundary cropping, historical-data cities and trainability annotations in Figure 2. Its abstract explicitly points to code as well as datasets at the existing project address. DNCM reference-selection details and k=32 are removed. Core hardware, training and sampling details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds DDPM, CrossViewDiff and Geospecific View Generation citations, while removing HawkI and Neural Preset for Color Style Transfer. It explicitly distinguishes the already-cited GPG2A work by its existing BEV transformation and one-to-one restriction. Publication updates to retained references do not represent new works.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, diffusion and dataset explanations are rewritten, and training and implementation details are consolidated. G2A-3 task subsections are reordered and its results receive a separate Section 5.4 after the ablations. The overall six-section narrative and much of the prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 2 and 4 are substantially redrawn, and the G2A-3 qualitative display is reduced and reorganized with different examples and no ControlNet column. The ablation table changes from component checkboxes to named variants. Tables 2–3 exchange roles and locations; the multi-view figure moves unchanged from Figure 7 to Figure 6.

improvement.justification: The standard-BEV controls address an important attribution gap, and GPG2A adds a relevant comparison. However, v4 assigns v3's light-assisted multi-view scores to a row without that condition, weakening traceability. G2A-3 ControlNet scores also remain identical despite the reported split revision. The PDFs do not explain these discrepancies sufficiently to weigh the stronger evaluation design against the loss of experimental clarity.
